{{Short description|Italian inorganic chemist}}
'''Carlo Floriani''' was an [[inorganic chemist]] who gained renown for contributions to [[organometallic]] and [[coordination chemistry]]. He was born in Casalmaggiore, Cremona ([[Italy]]) in 1940 and died in 2005.  He held positions at the [[University of Pisa]], [[Columbia University]], and [[EPFL|Ecole Polytechnique, Lausanne]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Floriani, Carlo |url=https://www2.unil.ch/elitessuisses/personne.php?id=79469}}</ref>  He had been a protoge of [[Fausto Calderazzo]].<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1021/om5011963 |title=Fausto Calderazzo: Pioneer in Mechanistic Organometallic Chemistry |date=2014 |last1=Maitlis |first1=Peter M. |last2=Belli Dell'Amico |first2=Daniela |journal=Organometallics |volume=33 |issue=24 |pages=6989–7006 }}</ref>

[[Image: Fe2mes4.png|thumb|right|Structure of Tetramesityl diiron, first prepared by the Floriani group.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Klose | first1 = Alain | last2 = Solari | first2 = Euro | last3 = Floriani | first3 = Carlo | last4 = Chiesi-Villa | first4 = Angiola | last5 = Rizzoli | first5 = Corrado | last6 = Re | first6 = Nazzareno | year = 1994 | title = Magnetic Properties Diagnostic for the Existence of Iron(II)-Iron(II) Bonds in Dinuclear Complexes Which Derive from Stepwise Insertion Reactions on Unsupported Iron-Aryl Bonds | journal = J. Am. Chem. Soc. | volume = 116 | issue = 20| pages = 9123–9135 | doi = 10.1021/ja00099a030 }}</ref>]]

His contributions included small molecule activation including [[carbon dioxide complex]]es and [[dinitrogen complex]]es.  He prepared several transition metal mesityl complexes such as [[tetramesityldiiron]] and gold mesityl.

He was recognized with the Centenary Prize, Royal Society of Chemistry.
